issues.passage: He felt such affinity for the rival proposal that he blocked any further discussion of it.
issues.why: "Felt affinity for" is correct, natural use of affinity = natural liking/connection. The second clause is only pragmatically odd (liking something yet blocking talk of it); it does not make the word itself a misuse. A student who knows the definition would rightly accept this passage.

fix.correctPassage: She felt an immediate affinity for the spare, geometric style of the paintings.
wrongPassages: Signing the contract created a legal affinity requiring delivery by the end of June.
Surveyors recorded the affinity between the two property lines before building the fence.
The mayor issued a formal affinity barring the developer from the hearing.
